rapport_notes: Joanna is warm, patient with customer confusion, uses the customer's name, and handles tangential questions gracefully.
process_discipline_notes: No silence held after 'Does that make sense?' (immediate pivot to cost breakdown); no explicit close ask or rate-lock line at end of call.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: we actually just wanna ask some questions about this move so we can give you a more personalized estimate but of course I'll send everything in the email as well after our call — framing present but no explicit time-box or accuracy promise
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep launches directly into logistics probing (addresses, floor, furniture, boxes) without asking 'what are your biggest concerns' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised concerns (monitors/fragile items, TV mounting) late in discovery, but rep acknowledged without follow-up — 'Yup, that's okay, no worries' → pivot. No second-layer probing on any concern.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: we also include other features like our no worries, damage coverage that would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages — covered in Stage 2 as part of features pitch (valid slot)
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: meet your mover feature. Rest assured we don't take daily contract to workers. Our guys are the most of Ved movers in the industry, and we'll send you their names ahead of time to let you know who's coming to help out with the move — covered in Stage 2 (valid slot)
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: on time guarantee if we run late on the time we schedule, we provide discounts by the end of the day — covered in Stage 2
evidence_quotes.communication_not_covered: No mention of day-before call, named crew lead, or inbox updates anywhere in the call
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: typically a one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours to complete now. Of course since we're moving to one bedroom apartments we are already at the range of five to seven hours now... I'll just quote your move one, the six to eight hour mark with three men involved — range provided and personalized to the two apartments + walking distances
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_window: how we work Clarissa is that, of course the shorter than move is gonna be then the lower the cost at the end of the day... you only pay for how long it will take after the two and a half hour minimum is met — window logic explained
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: if the guys would be able to finish everything within six hours, that will be an estimated budget of $1,906. If it goes up to eight hours, that would be a ho $2,518 again at the end of the day you only pay for how long it will take... we only charge in fifteen minute increments — covered
evidence_quotes.self_prep_tip_missing: No mention of 'anything you get done before we show up comes off your bill'
evidence_quotes.does_that_feel_fair_silence: 'Does that make sense?' is asked but immediately followed by pivot — no silence held: 'Alright now, typically a one bedroom apartment...'
evidence_quotes.close_missing: Call ends with 'I'll go ahead and send you an updated quotation' and 'I'll talk to you later' — no rate-lock line ('your rate locks when you book') and no explicit ask ('would you like our help with your move?')

top_strength: Joanna managed two complex addresses and a multi-step move (two apartments → one destination) with clear, methodical logistics probing, captured all room/furniture details accurately, and gracefully handled customer interruptions and clarifications.
coaching_note: Ask 'other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' early (after quid pro quo, before logistics probing) — this is the single highest-priority line in the script; it unlocks discovery depth and positions the differentiators, and it was never asked here.
